verdict_reason: The current valid-domain kernel computes its disclosed BLME proxy faithfully: on a non-tied construction, the live evaluator and an independent SciPy cosine-distance/argpartition implementation both returned stability_mean=0.8997190024587284 and stability_std=0.1040103180107919 (absolute differences 0.0). The direction-normalized perturbation realized relative norm 0.03700000047683716 with sd 2.31e-9 for requested 0.037, while self-reference returned mean/std=1.0/0.0; I found no value-changing counterexample on the claimed same-token checkpoint or seeded-noise domains.
comparable_reason: Raw cross-width comparison fails a direct isometry test. Zero-padding the identical GPT-2 embedding geometry from D=768 to 1024/1280/2048 preserved sampled cosine Gram entries exactly (max abs difference 0.0) yet changed 10-seed mean stability from 0.9506545 to 0.9583652/0.9613461/0.9671573 (Spearman(D, score)=1.0); the +0.0165028 shift is 33.4% of the original instability and 0.64 of the observed score sd across 11 real models. At D=2048 only 0.612206 of the normalized noise lies in the original 768-dimensional subspace, matching sqrt(768/2048)=0.612372, so different widths are not receiving the same neighborhood-level perturbation even though every row receives the same 1% L2 kick.
github_reason: I located the authors' 31-commit repository and its documented stability.py, but a fresh local clone failed with git exit 128 because this sandbox cannot connect to GitHub, so I did not claim executable parity. The released/paper statistic uses top-10 overlap o/k, whereas BLME deliberately reports J=o/(2k-o): at k=10 and o=4 these are 0.4 and 0.25 respectively, confirming the disclosed monotone per-item transform but not a like-for-like implementation of the released quantity.
paper_reason: Wendlandt et al.'s Table 1 publishes a three-space example with pairwise overlaps 4/10, 3/10, and 5/10, whose mean is 0.400000. Applying BLME's Jaccard separately gives 0.25, 0.1764706, and 0.3333333, mean 0.25326797 (-36.683%); because BLME is explicitly a k=50 seeded-noise/checkpoint proxy rather than the paper's k=10 independently-trained-space mean overlap, the paper supplies no number this task is supposed to reproduce.
confounds_reason: On 11 locally cached models at k=50, 800 sampled rows and seed 42, stability spanned 0.902660-0.987321 with Spearman rho=+0.237 for d_model, -0.248 for n_layers, and -0.327 for vocab_size; Pearson r with vocab_size was -0.858 (p=0.000719). More decisively, within-family rho(score,d_model) was +0.949 for GPT-2, +1.000 for Pythia, and +0.866 for Qwen, and the exact-geometry zero-padding intervention moved the score +0.016503 with rho=1.0, so ambient width is a causal confound even though the pooled 11-model rank correlation is modest.
defects: COMPARABILITY / DESIGN: ambient-isotropic fixed-L2 noise is not invariant to zero-padding. With GPT-2 cosine geometry unchanged to max abs 0.0, D=768 -> 2048 raises stability 0.9506545 -> 0.9671573 over 10 seeds; the raw output must not be treated as width-comparable.

CODE (optional reference mode): rows are aligned only by integer ID and vocabulary length. Presenting the same 401 token embeddings under a permuted ID ordering returned 0.0132126 +/- 0.0248606 instead of the string-aligned answer 1.0 +/- 0.0; enforce tokenizer identity for checkpoint comparisons or align by token string.

PROTOCOL: one seed is the complete perturbation estimate and stability_std is token-row dispersion, not seed uncertainty. On fixed GPT-2 geometry with 128 rows, 10 complete seeded runs ranged 0.945174-0.954905 with across-seed sd 0.003132.
